<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
squashmigrations does not unset model options when optimizing CreateModel and AlterModelOptions
Description
	
When an operation resembling AlterModelOptions(name="test_model", options={}) is squashed into the corresponding CreateModel operation, model options are not cleared on the resulting new CreateModel operation object.
CreateModel.reduce() sets the new options as options={**self.options, **operation.options} in this case (django/db/migrations/operations/models.py line 144 on commit 991dce4f), with no logic to remove options not found in operation.options as is found in AlterModelOptions.state_forwards().
I believe this issue still exists on the master branch based on my reading of the code, but I've only tested against 2.2.

</pr_description>

                    fields=self.fields,
                    options=options,
                    bases=self.bases,
                    managers=self.managers,
                ),
            ]"""

content = content.replace(old, new)

    f.write(content)
EOF

import django.db.migrations.operations.models as m

# Test 1: AlterModelOptions with empty options should clear ALTER_OPTION_KEYS
create = m.CreateModel('TestModel', fields=[], options={'ordering': ['name'], 'verbose_name': 'Test'})
alter = m.AlterModelOptions('TestModel', options={})
result = create.reduce(alter, 'myapp')
print('Test 1 - Result options:', result[0].options)
assert result[0].options == {}, f'Expected {{}}, got {result[0].options}'

# Test 2: AlterModelOptions changing one option should keep it, clear others
create = m.CreateModel('TestModel', fields=[], options={'ordering': ['name'], 'verbose_name': 'Test'})
alter = m.AlterModelOptions('TestModel', options={'ordering': ['-name']})
result = create.reduce(alter, 'myapp')
print('Test 2 - Result options:', result[0].options)
assert result[0].options == {'ordering': ['-name']}, f'Unexpected: {result[0].options}'

# Test 3: Non-ALTER_OPTION_KEYS options (like db_table, which is not in ALTER_OPTION_KEYS) should be preserved

alter = m.AlterModelOptions('TestModel', options={})
result = create.reduce(alter, 'myapp')
print('Test 3 - Result options:', result[0].options)
# db_table is not in ALTER_OPTION_KEYS, so it should be preserved
assert result[0].options == {'db_table': 'custom_table'}, f'Unexpected: {result[0].options}'

print('All tests passed!')
"
